      "pattern": "shock",
      "direction": "increase",
      "magnitude": "flat-topped pulse ~+0.27 over 2y (peak A/E 1.25, ~25% above expected); reverts to ~0.90-0.96 (slightly below baseline) in 2018-2020, then settles near 1.0",
      "confidence": 0.8,
      "evidence": [
        "ae_death_by_year.csv: 2016 A/E=1.250 (z+4.3), 2017 A/E=1.239 (z+4.4) — level held flat (flat top), not a gradual build-up; sharp step down in 2018 to 0.898 (z-2.0)",
        "computed pack [DEATH]: profile SHAPED-PULSE, excursion 2016-2017 (2y) +0.273 score 13.8; onset max-1yr-move/excursion = 1.25 (whole excursion arrives in ONE year); step -0.212 at 2018; 3y-MA amplitude 0.241 confined to the pulse",
        "overdispersion x3.22 = mild / normal texture (Poisson z-scores indicative only); per-year z of ~4.3-4.4 both years plus a 2-year flat hold and clear reversion exceed what that scatter would produce, so this is a level change (shock), not drift and not erratic dispersion",
        "rest of book clean: CI/TPD/IP yearly A/E all 0.96-1.05 with flat trends (R2<0.2); IP termination by diagnosis all |z|<=1.0; no cross-line coordinated swing across consecutive years"

      "recommended_action": "Treat as a one-off 2016-2017 death-claims level change and investigate the driver: pull 2016-2017 death claims & exposure to check for a single large group / large claim, a coding or data change, or a change in the expected-claims basis. If a one-off is confirmed, no pricing/valuation change; if an expected-basis change is found, correct the baseline. Log in the death experience review; no CI/TPD/IP follow-up needed."
    }
  ]
}

- Anomalies, when present, are one of:
  * drift: a sustained year-over-year move in A/E over 2+ years. A drift does

    not evidence against the trend that came before it. When reporting drift,
    set years to the FULL window of the trend INCLUDING the gentle early ramp
